historical_record.description: The Commission's schedule of dedications for six new or improved playgrounds of the 1947 recreation bond program included Longfellow Playground, renamed Alice Chalmers Playground, which its index records as dedicated on March 31.

The Recreation Commission awarded the contract to build the field house at Longfellow Playground, on Brunswick Street between Whittier and Lowell, to Wm. McIntosh & Son at $22,577, the lowest of five bids.
The Recreation Commission resolved that the new playground being built on the Longfellow Playground site be named, on completion, for Alice Chalmers, principal of Longfellow School for many years.

The Recreation and Park Commission gave conceptual approval to enlarging the field house at Alice Chalmers Playground, Brunswick and Whittier Streets, for its crowded tiny-tot and senior programs, designed by Peter Moy of Finger and Moy, architects, with a larger meeting room and kitchen, accessible restrooms and a clerestory to light the middle of the building.
